top_signals.title: AI Boom Forces Massive Investment in Power Grids Worldwide
top_signals.summary: The information technology industry is driving massive growth in global electricity demand, which is set to rise by more than 10,000 TWh over the next ten years. For this electricity to reach demand hubs, grids around the world will need urgent upgrades. The big question is who will pay for it. In its World Energy Outlook released this week, the International Energy Agency once again joined the growing chorus of forecasters warning that data centers are becoming a major drain on electricity supply. Some of these warnings and community opposition…

top_signals.title: Anthropic Fails to Calm AI Jitters, Ditching the Kitchen for Thanksgiving
top_signals.summary: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Just Ice Tea Co-Founders Seth Goldman & Spike Mendelsohn, Seaport Research Partners Managing Director & Chief Equity Strategist Jonathan Golub, The New Yorker Staff Writer Jon Lee Anderson and The Atlantic Contributing Writer & “The Best Kind of American” Author Kim Ghattas. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Britain's Net Zero Revolution Has a China Problem
top_signals.summary: The Labour government has been accused of “capitulation” in its trade relations with China as Britain’s transition to net zero faces a number of security risks. A new report, published shortly before President Trump’s momentous trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, has highlighted the UK’s dependence on China for net zero-related technology and potential vulnerabilities in supply chains.  Policy Exchange researchers found that China accounts for 91 per cent of the UK’s solar imports, plus…
